claims.text: Optimizing composition and processing conditions can convert the metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state into a stable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state.
Achieving the stable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state could improve combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance.
Solid-solution strengthening would contribute to improved mechanical properties.
Precipitation strengthening would contribute to improved mechanical properties.
Grain refinement would contribute to improved mechanical properties.
The combined effects of solid-solution strengthening, precipitation strengthening, and grain refinement would improve corrosion resistance.
The combined effects of solid-solution strengthening, precipitation strengthening, and grain refinement would improve high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The proposed alloy must retain a density below 6 g/cm3.
The exact composition and processing conditions needed to achieve the proposed optimal state are unknown.
